headline: Burkina Faso Marks Major Victory Against Malaria
meta_description: Two years after vaccine introduction, Burkina Faso reports 32% drop in malaria cases and 44% reduction in deaths.
summary_short: Burkina Faso celebrates a dramatic decline in malaria cases and deaths following the rollout of a new vaccine, with particularly strong results among young children.
body:
Two years after introducing a malaria vaccine, Burkina Faso has recorded a 32% decrease in malaria cases and a 44% drop in deaths, according to Health Minister Robert Kargougou.

The impact on the country's youngest and most vulnerable population is striking. Among children under five, cases fell by 39% while mortality declined by more than 40%. These figures underscore how the vaccine has shifted the burden of disease in one of Africa's regions hardest hit by malaria.

The vaccine rollout represents a turning point for public health in Burkina Faso, where malaria has long been a leading cause of illness and death. With sustained vaccination efforts, these early gains suggest a pathway toward further progress in protecting children and reducing the disease's grip on communities across the country.
quick_facts: 32% decrease in recorded malaria cases in Burkina Faso
44% reduction in malaria deaths over two years
39% decline in cases among children under five
Health Minister Robert Kargougou announced the results
Mortality fell over 40% in children under five
